The graph of the function $y=f(x)$ is shown above. Approximate ${f}^{′}(x)$ at the point $x=4$ using a central difference approximation with step size $h=1.$

*Hint: Assume that the graph passes through the points with integer $y$-coordinates when $x=3$ and $x=5.$*

${f}^{′}(4)≈$
{{field-1}}
worked_solution:
We use the central difference approximation

$$
{f}^{′}(x)≈\frac{f(x+h)-f(x-h)}{2h},
$$

at the point $x=4$ with step size $h=1.$ This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(4) & ≈\frac{f(4+1)-f(4-1)}{2(1)} \\  & =\frac{f(5)-f(3)}{2} \\  & =\frac{2-(-1)}{2} \\  & =\frac{3}{2} \\  & =1.5.\end{aligned}
$$
